subject: EAST
title: FYS: East Asian Culture
description: An introduction to East Asian culture based on close examination of primary and secondary texts as well as visual materials.

restrictions.text: Open only to newly admitted students in U0 or U1, who may take only one FYS.

notes: Note: Enrolment limit 25. Students who register for more than one FYS will be obliged to withdraw from all but one of them
Note: Language of instruction is English.

subject: EAST
title: Introduction: East Asian Culture: China
description: This course provides a critical introduction to central themes in Chinese culture. The course will also examine the changing representations of the Chinese cultural tradition in the West. Readings will include original sources in translation from the fields of literature, philosophy, religion, and cultural history.

subject: EAST
title: Introduction: East Asian Culture: Japan
description: An introduction to Japan which presents various aspects of Japanese literature, culture, history, religions, philosophy and society.

subject: EAST
title: Introduction: East Asian Culture: Korea
description: This course provides a critical introduction to central themes in Korean culture, including Korean literature, religions, philosophy, and socio-economic formations.

subject: EAST
title: Introduction to East Asian Art
description: Introductory survey of some of the major developments in the visual arts of Japan, China, and Korea. Emphasis will be placed on the diversity of artistic traditions in East Asia and the intersections among these traditions.

restrictions.text: Not open to students taking or who have taken ARTH 215.

subject: EAST
title: Introduction to Global Asia
description: Explores Asia as a global force shaped by migration, exchange, and transnational networks. Traces movements of people, ideas, and media—from Buddhist pilgrims and overseas students to diasporas and pop culture—revealing Asia’s central role in world history and contemporary globalization. Examines themes of nation, identity, race, gender, and translation through literature, history, theory, and film, highlighting how Asia has both shaped and been shaped by global interactions.

subject: EAST
title: First Level Korean
description: Introduction to the basic structures of the standard Korean language. The aim of this course is to give students a basic knowledge of the Korean language. Special emphasis is put on handling everyday conversation, reading and writing short texts, and mastering basic grammar rules.
notes: An activities fee of $106.06 is charged to support the cost of visits to a Kimchi factory, restaurant meals, theatrical demonstrations, and explorations in the cultural richness of the language.

subject: EAST
title: First Level Chinese
description: Introduction to the basic structures of Mandarin Chinese, Pin-yin romanization and 750 characters for reading and writing. Emphasis on developing aural and oral skills through communication games and interaction activities. Animated films are used as part of teaching materials.
notes: An activities fee of $153.96 is charged to support the cost of visits to museums, restaurant meals, theatrical demonstrations, and explorations in the cultural richness of the language.

subject: EAST
title: First Level Japanese
description: Introduction to the basic grammar and sentence patterns of the Japanese language in both oral and written forms. In reading and writing skills students will be introduced to katakana, hiragana and kanji.
notes: An activities fee of $189.88 is charged to support the cost of visits to museums, restaurant meals, theatrical demonstrations, and explorations in the cultural richness of the language.

subject: EAST
title: Japanese Writing Beginners 1
description: Grammar, vocabulary, kanji, and introduction ofsome new expressions.

prerequisites.text: EAST 240 or equivalent or permission of the instructor

notes: Language of instruction: Japanese and English.

subject: EAST
title: Japanese Writing Beginners 2
description: Grammar, vocabulary, kanji, and introduction ofsome new expressions.

prerequisites.text: EAST 240 or EAST 241 or equivalent or permission of the instructor

notes: Language of instruction: Japanese and English.

subject: EAST
title: Introduction to Asian Media Studies
description: The course explores core methods and theoretical approaches to media in Asia and beyond: material culture, technicity, media infrastructures, intermediality, circulation, platforms, regionalism, and institutional history.

subject: EAST
title: Introduction to Film History
description: An introduction to representative periods, movements and styles in the history of cinema, as well as questions of film historiography.

restrictions.text: Not open to students who have taken or are taking FILM 279 or LLCU 279

notes: Language of instruction: English.

subject: EAST
title: Borderlands of Modern China
description: Investigation of the relationship of China to its frontiers from the Qing Dynasty to the present, examining the history and cultural and literary production of regions like Manchuria, Mongolia, Tibet, Xinjiang, southwestern China, Taiwan, and Hong Kong as well as Chinese depictions of and approaches to these regions. Explores how China came to take its present geographical form while exploring questions of ethnicity, religion, language, and colonialism.

restrictions.text: Not open to students who have taken EAST 303 when topic was "Borderlands of Modern China".

notes: Recommended: EAST 211 or HIST 208 or HIST 218

subject: EAST
title: Rebellion and Revolution in Modern China
description: Exploration of the role of rebellion and revolution in shaping 19th and 20th century China. Covers major movements like the Taiping, the Boxers, the Kuomintang, and the Chinese Communist Party, with attention to their political, social, and cultural impact.

restrictions.text: Not open to students who have taken HIST 328 when the topic was "Rebellion and Revolution in Modern China".

notes: Recommended: EAST 211 or HIST 208 or HIST 218

subject: EAST
title: Second Level Korean
description: The aim of this course is to give students a fluent speaking ability in daily conversation, advanced grammar knowledge, improved reading and writing skills. Special emphasis is put on the efficient use of grammar, enrichment of vocabulary, and mastering useful expressions encountered in everyday life.

prerequisites.text: EAST 220 or equivalent

notes: Students must register for both EAST 320D1 and EAST 320D2.
No credit will be given for this course unless both EAST 320D1 and EAST 320D2 are successfully completed in consecutive terms

subject: EAST
title: Archaeology East Asian Empires
description: An examination of utilitarian and elite objects, art, architecture, cities and tombs from the early to medieval period dynastic states (ca. 221 BCE1-279 CE) to gain understandings of developments and changes in economic organization, art, religion, political orgranization, internal interactions, and external connections, along with both elite and commoner life based on recent archaeological discoveries and research. Issues in archaeological practices and theories, and the use of received texts to understand the past will also be examined.

restrictions.text: Not open to students who have taken ANTH 328.

subject: EAST
title: Second Level Chinese
description: The same communicative approach as in EAST 230 is used to develop aural and oral skills on daily topics. In addition to textbooks, Chinese films on videotapes will be incorporated as teaching materials.

prerequisites.text: EAST 230 or equivalent or permission of the instructor

notes: Students must register for both EAST 330D1 and EAST 330D2.
No credit will be given for this course unless both EAST 330D1 and EAST 330D2 are successfully completed in consecutive terms

subject: EAST
title: Second Level Japanese
description: Continuation of the study of oral and written Japanese.

prerequisites.text: EAST 240 or equivalent or permission of instructor

notes: Students must register for both EAST 340D1 and EAST 340D2.
No credit will be given for this course unless both EAST 340D1 and EAST 340D2 are successfully completed in consecutive terms

subject: EAST
title: Japanese Writing Intermediate 1
description: Intermediate grammar, vocabulary and kanji,focusing on writing skills and reading comprehension.

prerequisites.text: EAST 340 or equivalent or permission of the instructor

notes: Language of instruction: Japanese.

subject: EAST
title: Japanese Writing Intermediate 2
description: Intermediate grammar, vocabulary and kanji, focusing on writing skills and reading comprehension.

prerequisites.text: Prerequisite(s): EAST 340 or EAST 341 or equivalent or permission of the instructor

notes: Language of Instruction: Japanese

subject: EAST
title: Gender and Sexuality in Chinese Literature
description: Gender and sexuality in modern and/or premodern Chinese literature with emphasis on representation of gender relations, notions of masculinity and femininity, morality and sexuality. Readings from fiction, drama, poetry, and/or other genres are approached from a variety of critical perspectives.

prerequisites.text: EAST 211 or permission of instructor.

notes: Note: Readings in English translation.

subject: EAST
title: Women Writers of China
description: A study of fiction, drama, and poetry by women writers in imperial, modern, and/or contemporary China.

prerequisites.text: EAST 211 or permission of instructor.

notes: Core course for the Women's Studies program

subject: EAST
title: Critical Approaches to Chinese Literature
description: This course will examine traditional and/or modern genres of Chinese literature with a focus on different forms of Chinese and Western literary analysis.

prerequisites.text: EAST 211.

subject: EAST
title: Approaches to Chinese Cinema
description: Development of Chinese film in the 20th century, with an emphasis on both critical approaches to film as well as film history.

prerequisites.text: EAST 211.

subject: EAST
title: Early Chinese Art
description: Survey of Chinese art and visual culture during the pre-imperial and early imperial periods (1500BCE-900CE). A wide range of visual images and media (painting, architecture, inscription, funerary art) will be examined in the historical context of the rise and development of the empire.

prerequisites.text: One 200-level Art History or East Asian Studies course, or by permission of instructor.

restrictions.text: Not open to students taking or who have taken ARTH 357.

subject: EAST
title: Animation and New Media
description: Animation and new media in East Asia, with an emphasis on postwar developments.

restrictions.text: Not open to students who have taken EAST 214.

subject: EAST
title: Japanese Cinema
description: This course will study the development of film in Japan during the 20th century with a particular focus on the analysis of film form, genres and history.

subject: EAST
title: Early and Medieval Japan
description: This course examines cultural production in early and medieval Japan, focusing on calligraphy, painting, picture scrolls, gestures and their relation to textual production. Readings explore various classic texts, taboos against seeing and narrative modes of cognition.

prerequisites.text: EAST 212 or permission of instructor

subject: EAST
title: Mass Culture and Postwar Japan
description: This course addresses a number of analytic approaches to mass culture in order to examine the culture industry of post-war Japan. Emphasis on narrative strategies in popular or consumer fiction and on the problems of marginalized writers.

prerequisites.text: Any introductory course in literature or cultural studies, or permission of instructor

subject: EAST
title: Asian Genre Cinemas
description: This course explores the historical and aesthetic dimensions of Asian genre cinemas in a regional framework, in relation to varied social and cultural phenomena. Genres explored include the gangster film, martial arts action, horror, revenge, melodrama, period drama, and documentary.

subject: EAST
title: Gender and Sexuality in Asian Media
description: In this course, we examine contesting notions of gender, sexuality, femininity, and masculinity in Asian cinema and media. We study how individual works negotiate the social discourses on gender and sexual representation, identities, and performance, and how we may borrow conceptual frameworks from queer theories and histories at large to discuss them.

subject: EAST
title: History of Sexuality in Japan
description: Social and cultural history of sexuality in Japan. Possible topics include pre-modern sexuality and relations to court, religion and anthropology; pre-modern sex and gender relations; modern sexuality and gender identities; sexuality and the rise of science; relation to nationalism; feminism and queer movements.

subject: EAST
title: Topics in Television: Asia
description: This course approaches television and televisuality historically, in regional, transnational, and global perspectives.

prerequisites.text: A 200-level course in EAST or permission of instructor.

subject: EAST
title: Korean Media and Popular Culture
description: This course approaches popular culture and mass media in postwar Korea from historical and theoretical perspectives, with a focus on the connections between activism, mass media, and commodity culture.

prerequisites.text: EAST 213 or permission of the instructor.

subject: EAST
title: Topics: Transnational Asian Culture
description: Investigation of cinema's border-crossing modes of cultural production, reception, and circulation, to uncover the ways that the study of culture enriches current theories and approaches to the transnational.

prerequisites.text: A 200-level course in EAST or permission of instructor.

subject: EAST
title: Asian Migrations and Diasporas
description: Introduction to the interdisciplinary study of Asian migrations and diasporas. Topics include colonialism and diaspora, transnationalism, globalization, citizenship, migration and the state, gender and migration, human trafficking, and forced migration.

subject: EAST
title: Age of Samurai
description: Examination of the history, society, and culture of early modern Japan in the period of rule by the warrior class: the samurai. Examination of the formation and collapse of the samurai-dominated political order of the Tokugawa shogunate, as well as themes like social status, gender and sexuality, religion, and connections to the outside world during the period of Tokugawa rule.

restrictions.text: Not open to students who have taken HIST 443 or EAST 493 when the topic was "Age of Samurai".

notes: Recommended: EAST 212 or HIST 208 or HIST 218

subject: EAST
title: Martial Tradition in Chinese Literature and Culture
description: China's martial tradition; themes such as war, revenge, justice, and the use of violence, alongside martial arts. Topics include: philosophical discourses on war, literary nationalism, and representations of these themes in literature, film, digital media, and games. Spanning from the 6th century BCE to the 20th century, the key periods and genres of Chinese literature and martial traditions beyond popular media.

prerequisites.text: Recommended: EAST 211

restrictions.text: Not open to students who have taken EAST 453 when topic was "The Martial Tradition in Chinese Literature and Culture".

subject: EAST
title: Third Level Korean 1
description: grammar, enhancing written and oral comprehension and improving writing and speaking skills.

restrictions.text: Not open to students who have taken or are taking EAST 420D1/D2.

subject: EAST
title: Third Level Chinese
description: A communicative approach will be used to provide students with skills to communicate in various situations, express their ideas and feelings, and discuss various aspects of culture and life in China and in Canada. Teaching materials include Chinese movies on videotape and slides depicting Chinese life and culture.

prerequisites.text: EAST 330 or equivalent or permission of instructor

notes: Students must register for both EAST 430D1 and EAST 430D2.
No credit will be given for this course unless both EAST 430D1 and EAST 430D2 are successfully completed in consecutive terms

subject: EAST
title: Third Level Japanese
description: More advanced study of the Japanese language. Emphasis will be placed on reading.

prerequisites.text: EAST 340 or equivalent or permission of instructor

notes: Students must register for both EAST 440D1 and EAST 440D2.
No credit will be given for this course unless both EAST 440D1 and EAST 440D2 are successfully completed in consecutive terms

subject: EAST
title: Late Imperial China
description: Examination of Chinese society in the Ming and Qing eras (1368-1912) through the exploration of themes like gender and sexuality, family, law, ethnicity and borderlands, education, literary production, and political organization.

restrictions.text: Not open to students who have taken EAST 494 when the topic was "Late Imperial China" and not open to students who have taken or are taking HIST 445.

notes: Recommended: EAST 211 or HIST 208 or HIST 218

subject: EAST
title: Topics: Chinese Literature
description: Advanced seminar in selected genres, themes and issues in Chinese literature.

prerequisites.text: A 300-level course in any literature.

subject: EAST
title: Topics: Chinese Cinema
description: Advanced seminar in selected themes and issues in Chinese film.

prerequisites.text: EAST 353, a 300-level film studies course, or permission of the instructor.

subject: EAST
title: Inventing Modern Japanese Novel
description: An examination of the modern Japanese novel as a form which both affirms and resists the form of the European novel. Readings explore the particular problems of the Japanese novel in the context of modernization, westernization, and colonialism.

prerequisites.text: Any course in literature or cultural studies above the introductory level, or permission of instructor

subject: EAST
title: Japan in Asia
description: This course introduces theories of cultural interaction, interpellation, and intertexuality in order to reconsider Japanese modes of reception and selection of Chinese texts and technologies. Readings range from early Japanese to 20th century texts. Readings in translation.

prerequisites.text: Any East Asian Studies course above the introductory level, or permission of the instructor

subject: EAST
title: Image, Text, Performance
description: Drawing on theoretical approaches from a variety of cultural and media studies, including cinema, performance and performativity, and elsewhere, this course addresses cultural production in premodern and/or modern East Asia. Topics to be addressed range from calligraphy and writing, to theatre, and film.

prerequisites.text: Any East Asian Studies course above the introductory level, or permission of the instructor

subject: EAST
title: Topics: Japanese Cinema
description: Topics in the study of Japanese cinema.

prerequisites.text: EAST 362 or permission of the instructor.

subject: EAST
title: Science and Technology: Asia
description: History of science and technology in Asia with an emphasis on social and cultural impact and the legacy non-Western traditions.

prerequisites.text: EAST 211, EAST 212, EAST 213, or equivalent.

subject: EAST
title: Media and Environment in Asia
description: The course explores the intersection between media and "environment" in Asia and beyond; topics range from media ecology, cybernetics, environmental art and activism, urban planning, and the history of communications networks in Asia in the modern period.

prerequisites.text: Any East Asian Studies course at the 200 level or above.

description: Advanced seminar in the study of Korean film and media. Taught in English.

prerequisites.text: EAST 213 or permission of instructor.

subject: EAST
title: Seminar: Beyond Orientalism
description: Examines the cultural stakes and ethical implications of applying Western European models of understanding to East Asian societies. Provides background on interdisciplinary debates around "otherness", "cultural appropriation", and "postcolonialism", focusing on their history within East Asian Studies and their impact on that field's methodological assumptions, self-definition, and institutional practices.

prerequisites.text: any EAST course at the 300 level or above or permission of instructor

subject: EAST
title: Critical Area Studies in Asia
description: The course introduces students to foundational concepts, key debates, recent research areas, theoretical methods, and critical approached in area studies.

prerequisites.text: At least one EAST 400- or 500-level seminar course, or permission of the instructor.

subject: EAST
title: Fourth Level Chinese
description: Development of skills required to conduct academic discussions in oral as well as in written forms. Teaching materials include original texts from Chinese newspapers, Chinese literature and videos.

prerequisites.text: EAST 430 or equivalent

notes: Students must register for both EAST 530D1 and EAST 530D2.
No credit will be given for this course unless both EAST 530D1 and EAST 530D2 are successfully completed in consecutive terms
EAST 530D1 and EAST 530D2 together are equivalent to EAST 530

subject: EAST
title: Classical Chinese 1
description: An introduction to the grammar and syntax of classical Chinese. Readings are selected from well-known Confucian and Taoist classics, and philosophical and historical writings from premodern China.

prerequisites.text: EAST 330 or equivalent.

restrictions.text: Not open to students who have taken EAST 433.

subject: EAST
title: Chinese for Business 1
description: This course aims to provide advanced students of Chinese with training in the terminology and syntax necessary for business communications. Topics will include many different aspects of business negotiations, such as price negotiation, methods of payment, etc.

prerequisites.text: EAST 430D1 and EAST 430D2 or equivalent or permission of instructor.

subject: EAST
title: Chinese for Business 2
description: This course is a continuation of EAST 535. It is designed to further develop students' linguistic competence for business communication, and to provide students with some knowledge on China's trade policies as well as on different methods of trading with China.

prerequisites.text: EAST 535 or equivalent or permission of instructor

subject: EAST
title: Fourth Level Japanese
description: Advanced study of Japanese, with emphasis on reading Japanese newspapers. Classes will be conducted entirely in Japanese.

prerequisites.text: EAST 440 or equivalent or permission of instructor

notes: Students must register for both EAST 540D1 and EAST 540D2.
No credit will be given for this course unless both EAST 540D1 and EAST 540D2 are successfully completed in consecutive terms

subject: EAST
title: Classical Chinese Poetry Themes and Genres
description: A study of major themes and genres of classical Chinese poetry from its beginnings to the Yuan dynasty (14th century), with emphasis on critical analysis of text and context. Readings of poems in the original.

prerequisites.text: EAST 533 or permission of the instructor

subject: EAST
title: Technologies of Self in Early China
description: Readings on self-cultivation drawn from Confucian, Legalist, and Taoist philosophic texts of early China (5th-2nd centuries B.C.) in translation will be compared with historical and archaeological materials on the evolving construction of the "individual'' in Chinese social structure, military organization, political and ritual codes.

prerequisites.text: One advanced course in EAST or permission of the instructor

subject: EAST
title: Advanced Reading in Chinese
description: In-depth reading and analysis of advanced Chinese texts. Readings will be selected from a variety of prose genres ranging from fiction to journalistic writing.

prerequisites.text: EAST 430 or permission of instructor

subject: EAST
title: Advanced Translation: Chinese
description: Translation of Chinese texts into English or French. Materials will be selected from a variety of prose genres ranging from fiction to journalistic writing.

prerequisites.text: EAST 430 or equivalent or permission of instructor

subject: EAST
title: Advanced Topics: Chinese Literature
description: Consideration of selected topics and aspects of Chinese literature. The content of the course may vary from year to year, ranging from contemporary to modern to pre-modern literature.

prerequisites.text: one advanced course in EAST or permission of instructor

subject: EAST
title: Screen Cultures and Media Arts
description: This course explores the modern and contemporary screen cultures in Asia, analyzing media forms such as cinema, television, digital media and architecture through historical and theoretical frameworks. Emphasis will be placed on comparative approaches to media practices in Asia and beyond.

prerequisites.text: EAST 454; EAST 464 or EAST 467.

subject: EAST
title: Structures of Modernity: Asia
description: This course explores relations between some of the principal sites which structure the experience of "modernity" in Asia (and elsewhere) - from bodies and cities, to the urban context in general. Along with general approaches (e.g. the idea of everyday life; questions of time), specific topics may include speed, music, architecture, crime, etc.

prerequisites.text: EAST 453 or EAST 454 or EAST 462 or EAST 464 or EAST 477 or EAST 478; or permission of the instructor.

subject: EAST
title: Advanced Topics: Japanese Literature
description: Consideration of selected topics and aspects of Japanese literature. The content of the course may vary from year to year from contemporary to modern to pre-modern literature.

prerequisites.text: one advanced course in EAST or permission of instructor

description: Selected topics in the studies of pre-modern Asia (up to 1900).
notes: Students are expected to be equipped with their major research languages.

subject: EAST
title: Advanced Topics in Modern Culture and History in Asia
description: Selected topics in established and emergent analytical frameworks, and approaches to the study of cultural forms, sociopolitical and religious dynamics, and historical transformations of modern East Asia in context.
notes: Topic will vary from year to year

subject: EAST
title: Topics in Asian Visual Cultures
description: Examination of the contexts, theories, and methods of Asian visual cultures, including but not limited to the analysis of film, digital media, photography, print culture, and art. Special emphasis will be given to the development of Asian visual cultures from an interregionaland transpacific lens.
notes: Topic will vary from year to year

subject: EAST
title: Topics in Transnational Approaches to Asia
description: Exploration of critical humanities approaches to study cultural objects, social contexts, and historical conditions of East Asia and diasporic communities from transnational, transregional, and transpacific perspectives.
